description:
## Context

QuickHeadlines on FreeBSD crashes after 1-2 days of uptime with
excessive memory growth (observed: 9 GB VIRT after 1.5 h; 4.3 GB RSS
after 22 h; full system crash after 1-2 days). The in-progress
investigation quickhea-alz confirmed EventBroadcaster was leaking
client references; that fix landed in the previous commit
(c1a067d0). This epic enumerates the remaining suspected leak
vectors based on a code review against the principles in
planning/architecture.md (resource management, "Red Flags in Code:
Memory efficiency", bounded data structures).

## Suspected leak vectors (by file/area)

1. **feed_fetcher_concurrent.cr** — per-feed inner fibers are
   spawned via tracked_spawn (lines 42, 135) but the
   `result_channel = Channel(FeedData?).new(1)` allocation on
   line 133 is not GC-prompted; if the inner fiber holds it past
   the timeout (via closure capture of `feed`, `previous_feed_data`,
   `index`), it lingers. The outer fiber also holds the channel
   until the select completes. Per cycle: 1 outer + 1 inner fiber
   per feed (potentially hundreds of feeds). The FiberTracker
   counters should reflect this, but the *captured* state inside
   the fibers is what retains memory.

2. **favicon_storage.cr @client_pool** — Hash(String, HTTP::Client)
   keyed by host. Each unique feed host adds an HTTP::Client with
   its own socket pool / TLS context, never removed (only deleted
   on a single error path, line ~212). Grows unbounded as unique
   hosts are seen. The MemoryManagerActor cleanup paths do call
   `close_pooled_clients`, but only on emergency.

3. **socket_manager.cr** — Each registered connection spawns a
   per-connection writer fiber (line 342) that exits only when
   `outgoing.close` happens (line 351). If the websocket is
   half-closed (NAT timeout, client crash) but `closed?` returns
   false, the writer fiber is stuck on `websocket.send` and holds
   the `Connection` (which includes `outgoing` Channel +
   `CONNECTION_QUEUE_SIZE` worth of queued messages). Cleanup
   paths: handle_unregister_connection / handle_connection_closed
   are gated on the actor receiving a message, so a stuck writer
   that never errors never triggers cleanup.

4. **infrastructure/actor.cr _actor_call_with_timeout_json** —
   every def_call allocates a fresh `Channel(String).new(1)`
   (lines 257, 301). If the caller raises between
   `send_message` and `receive`, or under a 30s timeout, the
   channel + Call{Method} struct linger. With high call rates
   (rate limiter, memory manager, socket manager all per-request)
   this is hundreds of short-lived channels/minute. The
   RateLimiter has a positive-result cache (rate_limiter.cr) that
   mitigates most calls, but other callers (MemoryManagerActor
   get_rss_mb on every API request, SocketManager stats, etc.)
   still hit the actor.

5. **utils/string_pool.cr StringIntern** — MAX_POOL_SIZE=10000,
   eviction strategy removes oldest half. After eviction, the
   removed String keys are dereferenced but the same strings may
   still be held by FeedData via copy_with (state stores). Also:
   `StringIntern` only interns short strings; long RSS bodies are
   not interned, so this is bounded by content patterns not by
   feed count.

6. **gc_collector.cr maybe_collect** — 5-minute throttle, only
   invoked when supervisor calls it (line ~310) after each
   successful refresh cycle. If the refresh interval is 30 min
   and a cycle fails (memory critical pressure skip), no GC
   happens for 30+ min. Already tracked as quickhea-hwp.

7. **refresh_supervisor.cr run_timed_refresh** — On timeout
   branch (line ~288), `cancel_ch.send(nil)` signals the worker
   fiber but does NOT join it. The worker fiber continues
   running in the background, retaining `fetched_map` (potentially
   MB of parsed feed data) and the captured `config_snapshot`.
   The completion_channel sits un-acked.

8. **refresh_supervisor.cr run_initial_refresh** — Same pattern:
   cancel channel is set on `@state.initial_cancel_ch` but the
   `run_first_cycle` flow only signals cancellation at the very
   end of its sleep loop. If the initial refresh is slow
   (loading 100+ feeds from cold cache), the worker holds
   everything for 10+ minutes.

9. **app_state_service.cr @memory_history** — Capped at 500, OK.
   But `track_memory_usage` is gated on
   `@memory_history.size % 10 != 0`, which means tracking fires
   on every update only AFTER the array reaches size 10/20/...,
   then nothing until then. Semantically "every 10 updates"
   but the comment is misleading.

10. **event_broadcaster.cr @@client_history** — capped at 1000,
    OK (post-quickhea-alz fix).

11. **infrastructure/actor.cr mailbox** — bounded at 100 by
    default. If an actor is slow, callers block. Not a leak, but
    a slow actor under memory pressure causes `pending_threads`
    to grow in the calling fibers.

12. **quickheadlines.cr initiate_shutdown** — Spawns 4 separate
    `tracked_spawn` fibers for shutdown sequence; each holds
    closures capturing `SHUTDOWN_LOG`. Not a runtime leak
    (shutdown exits), but adds noise to FiberTracker stats.

## Goals

- Identify the dominant leak(s) with measurements, not guesses.
- Cap all unbounded data structures in the long-lived paths
  (connections, fibers, actor channels, HTTP clients).
- Add forced GC + per-cycle heap snapshots so future leaks are
  diagnosable in 10 min, not 22 h.
- Keep QuickHeadlines stable on FreeBSD for >= 7 days under
  nominal load with RSS under 1 GB.

## Acceptance

- Heap snapshots before/after each fix, RSS growth over 24 h
  < 100 MB on the same config as the FreeBSD production jail.
- All child tasks closed; bw sync clean.
- No new lints (ameba) and spec suite green.

## Sequencing

```mermaid
graph LR
  1[Add heap snapshot + RSS delta instrument] --> 2[Audit unbounded data structures]
  2 --> 3[Cap FaviconActor @client_pool]
  2 --> 4[Cap SocketManager writer fiber retention]
  2 --> 5[Cap actor reply channel lifetime]
  2 --> 6[Add periodic forced full GC backstop]
  3 --> 7[Long-running FreeBSD soak test 48h]
  4 --> 7
  5 --> 7
  6 --> 7
  1 --> 7
```
title: Memory leak investigation & fixes (1-2 day FreeBSD crash)
